_**User (2026-10-08 01:35:56Z)**_

Hey Claude, let's cook! As a quick summary, I am trying trying to implement a change for adding a draggable weekly calendar UI element for availability selection. The intent is to create a system similar to When2Meet or Google Calendar, where you can drag the mouse along a calendar grid to block off times of availability/unavability. The current system is based on text fields: you type a start and end time (there is a "plus" button to allow users to input non-contiguous blocks of availability). I will paste the full issue and spec below. Our first step should be to identify which code/files are relevant and to identify potential solutions to the issue. For context, this issue is ONLY about creating the UI element; future PRs will address the logic. ISSUE AND SPECS: 

<pasted_content id="7308">
### Summary
Create a new React component that renders a weekly grid with days of the week on the X-axis and hours (midnight to 11:59 PM) on the Y-axis. This serves as the foundational visual element for the drag-to-select availability feature.

### User story
As an event host, I want to see my weekly availability displayed across days and hours on an intuitive grid, so that I can clearly review my recurring open time slots.

### Rough scope
Medium — requires creating a responsive React grid component (7 days × 24 hourly rows), rendering time and day labels, implementing selected/unselected visual states driven by props, and embedding the component into the availability settings page layout. (Excludes drag interactions, data mutation, and backend/DB persistence).

### Source
Feature enhancement for availability configuration and foundational prerequisite for the drag-to-select scheduling interface.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Build and style the core weekly calendar grid component according to the following specifications:

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Grid displays 7 columns (days of the week: Sun–Sat) and 24 rows (hourly slots: 12:00 AM–11:00 PM).
- Time labels are rendered along the Y-axis.
- Day labels are rendered along the X-axis.
- Grid cells support distinct visual styles for "selected" and "unselected" states. 
- Component accepts availability state as a prop and renders the matching cell states accordingly.
- Component is fully responsive and integrates cleanly into the existing availability settings page layout.

**Out of scope:**
- Drag-and-drop / drag-to-select interactions.
- Data synchronization and API/DB persistence.

---

## Requirements Specification

## User Story
As a Cal.diy user, I want a visual weekly grid showing days and hours so that I have a spatial representation of my availability to interact with and so it is easier to input my availability.

## User Scenario
A user navigates to the availability settings page. Instead of seeing only text boxes, they see a 7-column, 24-row grid (exact numbers can be adjusted) with day labels across the top and hour labels down the left side. Cells that correspond to currently set available hours appear highlighted. The user can see their whole week's availability at a glance without reading any text fields.

Ultimately (the ideal implementation after the full completion of Issue #32), the user clicks and drags on the calendar to modify his availability. When the user toggles between calendar and text field mode, the user sees the same information.

## Acceptance Criteria
For now:
1. Grid renders 7 columns (Sun–Sat) with day labels on the X-axis
2. Grid renders 24 rows with hour labels (12:00 AM, 1:00 AM, … 11:00 PM) on the Y-axis
3. Cells have visually distinct "selected" and "unselected" states (e.g. filled vs. unfilled color); "distinct" may be hard to exactly specify, so let's say that the color and shading must be different between selected and unselected cells

## Out of Scope
- Drag-to-select interaction (Issue #70)
- Toggle between grid and text-field modes (Issue #71)
- Syncing grid state with text fields (Issue #73)
- Database reads/writes (Issue #73)

## Open Questions
- Should the Y-axis start at midnight or at a configurable earliest hour (e.g. 6:00 AM) to reduce whitespace?
- Should the appearance change based on the system settings (e.g. light vs dark mode)?
- How should the appearance change based on the size of the screen (e.g. phone vs computer)?
</pasted_content id="7308">

405	export function parseTimeString(input: string, timeFormat: number | null): Date | null {
406	  if (!input.trim()) return null;
407	
408	  const formats = timeFormat === 12 ? ["h:mma", "HH:mm"] : ["HH:mm", "h:mma"];
409	  const parsed = dayjs(input, formats, true); // strict parsing
410	
411	  if (!parsed.isValid()) return null;
412	
413	  const hours = parsed.hour();
414	  const minutes = parsed.minute();
415	
416	  if (hours < 0 || hours > 23 || minutes < 0 || minutes > 59) {
417	    return null;
418	  }
419	
420	  return new Date(new Date().setUTCHours(hours, minutes, 0, 0));
421	}

423	const LazySelect = ({

452	      setInputValue(newValue);
453	
454	      if (actionMeta.action === "input-change" && newValue.trim()) {

456	
457	        const formats = userTimeFormat === 12 ? ["h:mma", "HH:mm"] : ["HH:mm", "h:mma"];
458	        const parsedTime = dayjs(trimmedValue, formats, true);

461	        if (looksLikeTime && !parsedTime.isValid()) {

464	          const parsedDate = parseTimeString(trimmedValue, userTimeFormat);

468	            const violatesMax = max ? !parsedDayjs.isBefore(max) : false;
469	            setTimeInputError(Boolean(violatesMin || violatesMax));

473	        } else {

476	      } else {

480	    [userTimeFormat, min, max]
481	  );

483	  const filteredOptions = React.useMemo(() => {
484	    const dropdownOptions = options.filter((option) =>
485	      defaultFilter({ ...option, data: option.label, value: option.label }, inputValue)
486	    );
487	
488	    const trimmedInput = inputValue.trim();
489	    if (trimmedInput) {

492	      if (parsedTime) {

510	        }
511	      }
512	    }
513	
514	    return dropdownOptions;
515	  }, [inputValue, options, defaultFilter, userTimeFormat, min, max]);
516	
517	  const currentValue = dayjs(value).toDate().valueOf();
518	  const currentOption =

520	    (value
521	      ? {
522	          value: currentValue,

540	        if (!min && !max) filter({ offset: 0, limit: 0 });

558	interface IOption {
559	  readonly label: string;
560	  readonly value: number;
561	}
562	
563	/**
564	 * Creates an array of times on a 15 minute interval from
565	 * 00:00:00 (Start of day) to
566	 * 23:45:00 (End of day with enough time for 15 min booking)
567	 */
568	/** Begin Time Increments For Select */
569	const INCREMENT = Number(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AVAILABILITY_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL) || 15;
570	const useOptions = (timeFormat: number | null) => {
571	  const [filteredOptions, setFilteredOptions] = useState<IOption[]>([]);
572	
573	  const options = useMemo(() => {
574	    const end = dayjs().utc().endOf("day");
575	    const options: IOption[] = [];
576	    for (
577	      let t = dayjs().utc().startOf("day");
578	      t.isBefore(end);
579	      t = t.add(INCREMENT + (!t.add(INCREMENT).isSame(t, "day") ? -1 : 0), "minutes")
580	    ) {
581	      options.push({
582	        value: t.toDate().valueOf(),
583	        label: dayjs(t)
584	          .utc()
585	          .format(timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm"),
586	      });
587	    }
588	    // allow 23:59
589	    options.push({
590	      value: end.toDate().valueOf(),
591	      label: dayjs(end)
592	        .utc()
593	        .format(timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm"),
594	    });
595	    return options;
596	  }, [timeFormat]);
597	
598	  const filter = useCallback(
599	    ({ offset, limit, current }: { offset?: ConfigType; limit?: ConfigType; current?: ConfigType }) => {
600	      if (current) {
601	        const currentValue = dayjs(current).toDate().valueOf();
602	        const currentOption = options.find((option) => option.value === currentValue);
603	        if (currentOption) {
604	          setFilteredOptions([currentOption]);
605	        } else {
606	          // Create temporary option for custom time not in predefined options
607	          const customOption: IOption = {
608	            value: currentValue,
609	            label: dayjs(current)
610	              .utc()
611	              .format(timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm"),
612	          };
613	          setFilteredOptions([customOption]);
614	        }
615	      } else
616	        setFilteredOptions(
617	          options.filter((option) => {
618	            const time = dayjs(option.value);
619	            return (!limit || time.isBefore(limit)) && (!offset || time.isAfter(offset));
620	          })
621	        );
622	    },
623	    [options, timeFormat]
624	  );
625	
626	  return { options: filteredOptions, filter };
627	};

629	const getDateSlotRange = (endField?: FieldArrayWithId, startField?: FieldArrayWithId) => {
630	  const timezoneStartRange = dayjs((startField as unknown as TimeRange).start).utc();
631	  const nextRangeStart = dayjs((endField as unknown as TimeRange).end).utc();
632	  const nextRangeEnd =
633	    nextRangeStart.hour() === 23
634	      ? dayjs(nextRangeStart).add(59, "minutes").add(59, "seconds").add(999, "milliseconds")
635	      : dayjs(nextRangeStart).add(1, "hour");
636	
637	  const endOfDay = nextRangeStart.endOf("day");
638	
639	  if (!nextRangeStart.isSame(endOfDay)) {
640	    return {
641	      append: {
642	        start: nextRangeStart.toDate(),
643	        end: nextRangeEnd.isAfter(endOfDay) ? endOfDay.toDate() : nextRangeEnd.toDate(),
644	      },
645	    };
646	  }
647	
648	  const previousRangeStart = dayjs((startField as unknown as TimeRange).start).subtract(1, "hour");
649	  const startOfDay = timezoneStartRange.startOf("day");
650	
651	  if (!timezoneStartRange.isSame(startOfDay)) {
652	    return {
653	      prepend: {
654	        start: previousRangeStart.isBefore(startOfDay) ? startOfDay.toDate() : previousRangeStart.toDate(),
655	        end: timezoneStartRange.toDate(),
656	      },
657	    };
658	  }
659	};

661	const CopyTimes = ({
662	  disabled,
663	  onClick,
664	  onCancel,
665	  weekStart,
666	}: {
667	  disabled: number;
668	  onClick: (selected: number[]) => void;
669	  onCancel: () => void;
670	  weekStart: number;
671	}) => {
672	  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<number[]>([]);
673	  const { i18n, t } = useLocale();
674	  const itteratablesByKeyRef = useRef<(HTMLInputElement | HTMLButtonElement)[]>([]);
675	  useEffect(() => {
676	    document.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
677	    return () => {
678	      document.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
679	    };
680	  }, []);
681	  const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
682	    const itteratables = itteratablesByKeyRef.current;
683	    const isActionRequired =
684	      event.key === "Tab" || event.key === "ArrowUp" || event.key === "ArrowDown" || event.key === "Enter";
685	    if (!isActionRequired || !itteratables.length) return;
686	    event.preventDefault();
687	    const currentFocused = document.activeElement as HTMLInputElement | HTMLButtonElement;
688	    let currentIndex = itteratables.findIndex((checkbox) => checkbox === currentFocused);
689	    if (event.key === "Enter") {
690	      if (currentIndex === -1) return;
691	      currentFocused.click();
692	      return;
693	    }
694	    if (currentIndex === -1) {
695	      itteratables[0].focus();
696	    } else {
697	      // Move focus based on the arrow key pressed
698	      if (event.key === "ArrowUp") {
699	        currentIndex = (currentIndex - 1 + itteratables.length) % itteratables.length;
700	      } else if (event.key === "ArrowDown" || event.key === "Tab") {
701	        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % itteratables.length;
702	      }
703	      itteratables[currentIndex].focus();
704	    }
705	  };
706	
707	  return (
708	    <div className="stack-y-2 py-2">
709	      <div className="p-2">
710	        <p className="h6 text-emphasis pb-3 pl-1 text-xs font-medium uppercase">{t("copy_times_to")}</p>
711	        <ol className="stack-y-2">
712	          <li key="select all">
713	            <CheckboxField
714	              description={t("select_all")}
715	              descriptionAsLabel
716	              value={t("select_all")}
717	              checked={selected.length === 7}
718	              onChange={(e) => {
719	                if (e.target.checked) {
720	                  setSelected([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
721	                } else if (!e.target.checked) {
722	                  setSelected([]);
723	                }
724	              }}
725	              ref={(ref) => {
726	                if (ref) {
727	                  itteratablesByKeyRef.current.push(ref as HTMLInputElement);
728	                }
729	              }}
730	            />
731	          </li>
732	          {weekdayNames(i18n.language, weekStart).map((weekday, num) => {
733	            const weekdayIndex = (num + weekStart) % 7;
734	            return (
735	              <li key={weekday}>
736	                <CheckboxField
737	                  description={weekday}
738	                  descriptionAsLabel
739	                  value={weekdayIndex}
740	                  checked={selected.includes(weekdayIndex) || disabled === weekdayIndex}
741	                  disabled={disabled === weekdayIndex}
742	                  onChange={(e) => {
743	                    if (e.target.checked && !selected.includes(weekdayIndex)) {
744	                      setSelected(selected.concat([weekdayIndex]));
745	                    } else if (!e.target.checked && selected.includes(weekdayIndex)) {
746	                      setSelected(selected.filter((item) => item !== weekdayIndex));
747	                    }
748	                  }}
749	                  ref={(ref) => {
750	                    if (ref && disabled !== weekdayIndex) {
751	                      itteratablesByKeyRef.current.push(ref as HTMLInputElement);
752	                    }
753	                  }}
754	                />
755	              </li>
756	            );
757	          })}
758	        </ol>
759	      </div>
760	      <hr className="border-subtle" />
761	      <div className="flex justify-end space-x-2 px-2 rtl:space-x-reverse">
762	        <Button
763	          color="minimal"
764	          onClick={() => onCancel()}
765	          ref={(ref) => {
766	            if (ref) {
767	              itteratablesByKeyRef.current.push(ref as HTMLButtonElement);
768	            }
769	          }}>
770	          {t("cancel")}
771	        </Button>
772	        <Button
773	          color="primary"
774	          onClick={() => onClick(selected)}
775	          ref={(ref) => {
776	            if (ref) {
777	              itteratablesByKeyRef.current.push(ref as HTMLButtonElement);
778	            }
779	          }}>
780	          {t("apply")}
781	        </Button>
782	      </div>
783	    </div>
784	  );
785	};

export type TimeRange = {
  userId?: number | null;
  start: Date;
  end: Date;
};

export type Schedule = TimeRange[][];

/**
 * ```text
 * Ensure startTime and endTime in minutes since midnight; serialized to UTC by using the organizer timeZone, either by using the schedule timeZone or the user timeZone.
 * @see lib/availability.ts getWorkingHours(timeZone: string, availability: Availability[])
 * ```
 */
export type WorkingHours = {
  days: number[];
  startTime: number;
  endTime: number;
  userId?: number | null;
};

export type TravelSchedule = {
  id: number;
  timeZone: string;
  userId: number;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date | null;
  prevTimeZone: string | null;
};
import { getWeekdayNames, formatWeekday } from "./dateTimeFormatter";

type WeekdayFormat = "short" | "long";

export function weekdayNames(locale: string | string[], weekStart = 0, format: WeekdayFormat = "long") {
  const normalizedLocale = Array.isArray(locale) ? locale[0] : locale || "en";
  return getWeekdayNames(normalizedLocale, weekStart, format);
}

export function nameOfDay(
  locale: string | string[] | undefined,
  day: number,
  format: WeekdayFormat = "long"
) {
  const normalizedLocale = Array.isArray(locale) ? locale[0] : locale || "en";
  return formatWeekday(normalizedLocale, day, format);
}

69	        if (prevDefaultId !== currentDefaultId) {

} from "@calcom/features/schedules/components/ScheduleComponent";

>(props: {
  name: TPath;

  weekStart?: number;
  disabled?: boolean;

  userTimeFormat?: number | null;
}) => {

  return <ScheduleComponent userTimeFormat={timeFormat} {...props} />;
};

export default Schedule;

// Vitest 4.0 no longer allows custom CLI flags, so we use environment variables instead

const packagedEmbedTestsOnly = process.env.VITEST_MODE === "packaged-embed";
// eslint-disable-next-line turbo/no-undeclared-env-vars
const timeZoneDependentTestsOnly = process.env.VITEST_MODE === "timezone";
// eslint-disable-next-line turbo/no-undeclared-env-vars
const integrationTestsOnly = process.env.VITEST_MODE === "integration";
// eslint-disable-next-line turbo/no-undeclared-env-vars
const envTZ = process.env.TZ;
if (timeZoneDependentTestsOnly && !envTZ) {
  throw new Error("TZ environment variable is not set");
}

// Use pool: "forks" to prevent "Closing rpc while fetch was pending" errors.
const pool = "forks" as const;

const workspaces = packagedEmbedTestsOnly
  ? [
      {
        test: {
          name: "PackagedEmbedTests",
          include: ["packages/embeds/**/packaged/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js}"],
          environment: "jsdom",
          pool,

      },

import { useId } from "react";

import type dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { useTimePreferences } from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib";
import classNames from "@calcom/ui/classNames";

import type { BorderColor } from "@calcom/features/calendars/weeklyview/types/common";

export const HorizontalLines = ({
  hours,
  containerOffsetRef,
  borderColor,
}: {
  hours: dayjs.Dayjs[];
  numberOfGridStopsPerCell: number;
  containerOffsetRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement>;
  borderColor: BorderColor;
}) => {
  const { timeFormat } = useTimePreferences();
  // We need to force the minute to zero, because otherwise in ex GMT+5.5, it would show :30 minute times (but at the positino of :00)
  const finalHour = hours[hours.length - 1].add(1, "hour").minute(0).format(timeFormat);
  const id = useId();

  return (
    <div
      className={classNames(
        "pointer-events-none relative z-60 col-start-1 col-end-2 row-start-1 grid divide-y",
        borderColor === "subtle" ? "divide-subtle" : "divide-default"
      )}
      style={{
        gridTemplateRows: `repeat(${hours.length}, minmax(var(--gridDefaultSize),1fr)`,
      }}>
      <div className="row-end-1 h-(--calendar-offset-top) " ref={containerOffsetRef} />
      {hours.map((hour) => (
        <div key={`${id}-${hour.get("hour")}`}>
          <div className="text-muted sticky left-0 z-20 -ml-14 -mt-2.5 w-14 pr-2 text-right text-xs leading-5 rtl:-mr-14">
            {/* We need to force the minute to zero, because otherwise in ex GMT+5.5, it would show :30 minute times (but at the positino of :00) */}
            {hour.minute(0).format(timeFormat)}
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
      <div key={`${id}-${finalHour}`}>
        <div className="text-muted sticky left-0 z-20 -ml-14 -mt-2.5 w-14 pr-2 text-right text-xs leading-5 rtl:-mr-14">
          {finalHour}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

packages/lib/weekstart.ts
import { weekdayNames } from "./weekday";

// returns index of input weekName(long) from array starting from Sunday
// as fall back returns 0 i.e. Sunday
export function weekStartNum(weekName = "Sunday") {
  const weekDays = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"];
  const idx = weekDays.indexOf(weekName);
  return (idx !== -1 ? idx : 0) as 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;
}

// sorts the availability strings based on the weekStart
export function sortAvailabilityStrings(language: string, weekStart = "Sunday") {
  return (a: string, b: string) => {
    const weekNames = weekdayNames(language, weekStartNum(weekStart), "short");
    const weekIndex = (day: string) => {
      for (let i = 0; i < weekNames.length; i++) {
        if (day.includes(weekNames[i])) return i;
      }
      return -1;
    };
    return weekIndex(a) - weekIndex(b);
  };
}

/*
 * Detects navigator locale 24h time preference
 * It works by checking whether hour output contains AM ('1 AM' or '01 h')
 * based on the user's preferred language
 * defaults to 'en-US' (12h) if no navigator language is found
 */
import { localStorage } from "@calcom/lib/webstorage";

const is24hLocalstorageKey = "timeOption.is24hClock";

export enum TimeFormat {
  TWELVE_HOUR = "h:mma",
  TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR = "HH:mm",
}

export const setIs24hClockInLocalStorage = (is24h: boolean) =>
  localStorage.setItem(is24hLocalstorageKey, is24h.toString());

export const getIs24hClockFromLocalStorage = () => {
  const is24hFromLocalstorage = localStorage.getItem(is24hLocalstorageKey);

  if (is24hFromLocalstorage === null) return null;

  return is24hFromLocalstorage === "true";
};

export const getTimeFormatStringFromUserTimeFormat = (timeFormat: number | null | undefined): TimeFormat => {
  return timeFormat === 24 ? TimeFormat.TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR : TimeFormat.TWELVE_HOUR;
};

# Plan: Weekly availability grid UI (sub-issue of #32)

## Context
Availability is entered today as text-field time ranges (`ScheduleComponent` → `DayRanges` → `TimeRangeField`). Issue #32 adds a When2Meet / Google Calendar style grid that users can drag across, with a toggle between the two input modes. **This PR only builds the grid as a visual element**: it renders the current availability. Drag (#70), the toggle (#71), and two-way sync and persistence (#73) come later.

Decisions from discussion:
- **Slot precision matches the text fields (15 minutes).** The grid has 96 rows per day, with a label on each hour. The text fields and the grid should look like mirror images of the same data.
- **Only one mode is visible at a time.** The grid takes the place of the text-field Schedule inside the same card. It doesn't sit beside it or stack with it. The toggle button is #71's job.

## Design

### 1. Shared slot interval
`INCREMENT` in `packages/features/schedules/components/ScheduleComponent.tsx:569` isn't exported. Move it into a small constants file that both components import, so the grid and the dropdowns can't drift apart:
- `packages/features/schedules/lib/constants.ts`: export `AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (same env var and the same default of 15).
- Change `ScheduleComponent.tsx` to import it. Behavior stays the same.

### 2. Pure conversion util (the basis for #70 and #73)
`packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts`:
- `getSlotsPerDay(intervalMinutes)`: returns 1440 / interval.
- `scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule: TimeRange[][], intervalMinutes): boolean[][]`. It returns 7 rows (Sunday = index 0, matching the form) of `slotsPerDay` booleans.
  - A slot is selected if it falls inside any range, using the **UTC** hour and minute from `start`/`end`. That's how the form stores times (see `useOptions` in `ScheduleComponent`).
  - An `end` at 23:59 fills the last slot.
  - Use native `Date` / `getUTCHours`, not Day.js, because this runs in a loop.
  - Cost is O(ranges + slots) per day: compute the start and end indices for each range, then fill that span.
- #73 will later add the reverse function (`slotGridToSchedule`) here. It's not part of this PR.

### 3. Presentational component
`packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`. It's controlled by props and doesn't depend on tRPC, so it can live in `features` and the platform atom can use it.
```ts
type WeeklyAvailabilityGridProps = {
  value: boolean[][];            // 7 × slotsPerDay, Sunday-indexed
  weekStart?: 0|1|2|3|4|5|6;     // display rotation only
  timeFormat: number | null;     // 12 / 24
  intervalMinutes?: number;      // defaults to the shared constant
  className?: string;
};
```
- **Layout:** a CSS grid with an hour-label column plus 7 day columns.
  - Day headers come from `weekdayNames(i18n.language, weekStart, "short")` (`packages/lib/weekday.ts`), and the day index is `(i + weekStart) % 7`, the same rotation `ScheduleComponent` uses.
  - Hour labels appear only on full-hour rows and are formatted per `timeFormat` (`packages/lib/timeFormat.ts`).
- **Cells:**
  - Selected: `bg-brand-default`. Unselected: `bg-default`.
  - Hour lines use a solid `border-subtle`, quarter-hour lines a fainter dashed border.
  - Set `data-testid` and `data-selected` attributes for tests.
  - Add an `aria-label` per cell (day + time + "available"/"unavailable") so the grid is accessible.
- **Height:** 96 rows is tall, so the body sits in a vertical scroll container (`max-h-[600px] overflow-y-auto`) with a sticky day header.
- **Theme and mobile:**
  - Use semantic tokens only, so dark mode works automatically through `packages/config/theme/tokens.css`.
  - On narrow screens, columns shrink to `minmax(0,1fr)` with short day names. The label column stays narrow, and nothing scrolls horizontally.
- **Rendering cost:** 672 cells; wrap the component in `memo`.

### 4. Embedding in the page (the single swap point for #71)
In `packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx` (lines 668–701, the Schedule card):
- Add an optional prop `availabilityView?: "list" | "grid"` (default `"list"`). With `"grid"`, the card renders a thin wrapper that reads `useWatch({ name: "schedule" })`, converts it with `scheduleToSlotGrid`, and renders `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid` instead of `<Schedule>`.
- The default stays `"list"`, so platform-atom consumers and the live page don't change. #71 only needs to add the toggle and pass the prop down from `apps/web/modules/availability/[schedule]/schedule-view.tsx`.
- Replace the inline `indexOf` weekday array with `weekStartNum(weekStart)` (`packages/lib/weekstart.ts`) and reuse it for both components.

### 5. i18n
Add any new strings (cell aria-labels such as "available" / "unavailable", if those keys don't already exist) to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

## Files (about 6 code files, well under 500 lines)
- `packages/features/schedules/lib/constants.ts` (new)
- `packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts` (new) and `weekly-grid.test.ts` (new)
- `packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` (new) and `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.test.tsx` (new)
- `packages/features/schedules/components/ScheduleComponent.tsx` (import the constant)
- `packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx` (`availabilityView` prop and swap)
- `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`

## User Story
As an event host, I want to click and drag across a weekly grid to set my available hours instead of picking start and end times from individual dropdowns.

## User Scenario
A user navigates to their availability schedule and sees a visual weekly grid alongside the standard time dropdowns. They click and drag across the grid to highlight new available hours (e.g., Saturday 10:00–14:00) and click and drag over existing hours to remove them (e.g., a lunch break). Releasing the drag automatically updates the daily time ranges below. Once saved, the new schedule persists across both the grid and the list views.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A weekly grid displays the schedule, allowing users to click and drag to select or deselect time blocks with real-time visual highlighting.
2. Drag interactions work smoothly across both desktop and touch devices without accidental text selection, native drag artifacts, or page scrolling.
3. Releasing a drag automatically updates the corresponding daily time range inputs (merging adjacent blocks), enables the save button, and persists accurately to the database upon saving.
4. Automated tests must verify the conversion between grid cell selections and time ranges, and all new interface text must support translations.

## Out of Scope
- Date overrides 
- Keyboard-only selection on the grid (the existing day rows remain the keyboard-accessible method).

## Open Questions
- Should the grid replace the day rows, or appear next to them with a "Grid / List" toggle to preserve keyboard accessibility?
- What time increment should each cell represent (15 minutes vs 30 minutes)? A 15-minute increment results in a 96-row grid.
</pasted_content id="7308">

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 16:43:48Z)**_

Here's what each part of the plan does and how it builds on the text fields.

## How the grid relates to the text fields

The grid doesn't reuse the text-field UI components. It shares the **data** and the **settings** behind them:

| Shared | What it is | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Form field `schedule` | 7 days (Sunday = 0), each a list of `{start, end}` ranges, held by the page's form | This is the single source of truth. The text fields and the grid are two views of it. |
| Slot interval (`INCREMENT`) | The 15-minute step | The grid cells line up exactly with the dropdown options. |
| Week start | User preference, e.g. Monday first | Both views order the days the same way. |
| Time format | 12-hour or 24-hour preference | The labels match. |

The only change to the existing text-field code is one import, the shared constant. Everything else is new code beside it. Because both modes read and write the same `schedule` field, switching views later (#71) needs no extra syncing. The Save button and change detection already watch that field, which covers #70's "enables the save button" requirement.

## Design 1: what `INCREMENT` is

It's a constant at `ScheduleComponent.tsx:569`:
```ts
const INCREMENT = Number(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AVAILABILITY_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL) || 15;
```
It does two things in the text fields:
- It sets the spacing of the dropdown options (12:00, 12:15, 12:30, …).
- It sets how far the end time moves when you pick a start time (line 381).

A self-hoster can change it with an environment variable, for example to 30. If the grid hard-coded 15, it would stop matching the dropdowns. So the plan moves the constant into a shared file and both components import it. It's not exported today, which is why it has to move.

## Design 2: what `getSlotsPerDay()` does

It returns the number of rows per day: `1440 minutes / interval`. That's 96 at 15 minutes and 48 at 30 minutes. The grid uses it to know how many rows to draw. The conversion function uses it to size each day's list of true/false values (available or not).

One edge case: an interval that doesn't divide 1440 evenly, such as 7. I'd treat that as invalid and fall back to 15 rather than draw a partial last row.

`scheduleToSlotGrid` is the main piece. It turns the form's time ranges into a 7 × 96 table of available/unavailable slots. For example, Monday 9:00–17:00 becomes slots 36–67 set to true. #70 needs the reverse function, which turns slots back into merged ranges, and that function will sit next to it in the same file. #70's acceptance criterion 4 asks for tests on exactly this conversion, so keeping it as a plain function with no UI makes it easy to test.

## Design 3: assumptions behind the presentation

Each of these is a choice I made; any of them can change.

1. **96 rows, with labels only on the hour.** Lines on the hour are solid and quarter-hour lines are faint, so the grid stays readable.
2. **A fixed-height, scrolling area.** 96 rows at about 12px each is about 1,150px, taller than most screens. The grid scrolls inside a box of about 600px, and the day header stays fixed at the top.
3. **It starts at midnight**, as the parent issue specifies. A side effect is that the grid opens on midnight to early morning, which is mostly empty. **I'd add an automatic scroll to the first available slot, or to 8 AM, on load.** It's cheap and it isn't in the plan yet.
4. **No horizontal scrolling on mobile.** A phone is about 360px wide. That leaves roughly 45px for each of 7 columns after the label column, which is enough with short day names ("Mon"). The main reason is #70: on touch screens, a grid that scrolls both ways and also handles dragging creates conflicting gestures. #70's acceptance criterion 2 rules out page scrolling during a drag.
5. **Touch targets are small.** 12px rows are fine with a mouse but tight for a finger. That mainly affects #70, but row height is set here, so it's worth deciding now. One option is taller rows on touch devices.
6. **Day order follows the user's week-start setting.** It isn't always Sun–Sat. The default is Sunday, so it meets the spec, and it matches the text fields.
7. **Colors:** the brand color for available, the default background for unavailable. Theme color classes handle dark mode with no extra work.
8. **No timezone conversion.** The grid shows times in the schedule's own timezone, the same as the text fields.
9. **Each cell gets an accessible label**, e.g. "Monday 9:15 AM, available", even though #70 leaves keyboard selection out of scope.

## Design 4: the `"list"` / `"grid"` setting and the thin wrapper

You have the setting right. It defaults to `"list"`, so the live page doesn't change until #71 adds the toggle.

The wrapper connects the form to the grid. The grid itself only accepts a plain table of true/false values and knows nothing about the form. The wrapper:
1. reads the `schedule` field from the form,
2. converts it with `scheduleToSlotGrid`,
3. passes the result to the grid,
4. and in #70, writes drag results back with the reverse conversion.

Reasons to keep the grid separate from the form:
- **Testing:** the grid can be tested by passing a table directly, without setting up a whole form.
- **Re-render scope:** if `AvailabilitySettings` (786 lines) read the form field directly, the whole settings page would redraw on every change. During a drag in #70 that could mean dozens of redraws per second. With the wrapper, only the grid redraws.
- **Less wasted work:** the wrapper's form reading and conversion only run while the grid is showing.
- **A clean handoff:** #70 adds drag handling and write-back in the wrapper, and the grid's display code stays almost unchanged.

## Note from the #70 text

#70's scenario says the grid appears "alongside the standard time dropdowns" and updates "the daily time ranges below". That conflicts with your toggle decision, and its own open question asks "replace or toggle?". With the toggle, those ranges are hidden in grid mode but still update, because both views share the same form field. It's worth updating #70's wording so whoever picks it up isn't confused. Its other open question, 15 vs 30 minutes, is settled by following the shared interval.

Would you like me to add the auto-scroll on load and a decision on touch-friendly row height to the plan?

I updated the plan with your decisions. Here are the remaining answers.

## Plan changes from your feedback

**Interval rule (Designs 2 and 3.1).** I tightened it slightly. The interval must divide **60** evenly, not just 1440: 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 or 60. Anything else falls back to 15. Two reasons:
- Your rule is that hour lines stay solid with faint lines at each interval. That only works if every hour line falls on a cell boundary.
- An interval like 120 divides the day but not the hour. Each cell would then cross an hour line, and the labels would sit in the middle of cells.

Any interval that divides 60 also divides 1440, so your original rule is still covered. A new helper, `resolveSlotInterval`, applies this rule, and there are tests for the fallback cases.

**Row height (Design 3.5).** A percentage of the height won't work as-is. 96 rows inside a 600px box would be about 6px each, and the rows are meant to overflow the box and scroll. Instead:
- Each **hour** gets a fixed height, and each slot's height is that divided by the slots per hour.
- The grid is therefore the same total height whether the interval is 15 or 30 minutes.
- Hours are taller below the tablet breakpoint (e.g. 64px vs 48px), which gives you the taller rows on mobile.

**Starting scroll position (Design 3.3).** Nothing in the plan controls where the grid starts. It opens at midnight, and I noted auto-scroll as out of scope.

## Design 3.7: brand color and light/dark mode

**Brand color** is a color each user can set in **Settings → Appearance**, with separate values for light and dark mode. It colors their buttons and highlights. The default is near-black in light mode and white in dark mode. Using it for selected cells makes the grid match the rest of the user's Cal.diy styling.

**How light/dark mode works here.** We don't add any light/dark code. We use the existing system:
1. `packages/config/theme/tokens.css` defines named color variables, e.g. `--cal-brand` and `--cal-bg-subtle`, with light-mode values.
2. The same file has a `.dark { … }` block that redefines those variables with dark values.
3. When the user is in dark mode, the app puts a `dark` class on the page. That swaps every variable at once.
4. Tailwind classes like `bg-brand-default`, `bg-default` and `border-subtle` point at those variables, not at fixed colors.

So if the grid uses only those classes, it changes theme on its own, the same way the text fields do. The rule is never to hard-code a color like `#3b82f6` or `bg-blue-500`.

**One caveat to check visually.** In light mode the default brand color is near-black, so a fully selected 9–5 week becomes a large black block. If it looks too heavy, a lighter fill such as `bg-emphasis` or a semi-transparent brand color is a one-line change.

## Design 3.9: accessibility labels

Each cell gets an invisible text label, e.g. "Monday, 9:15 AM, available". Sighted users never see it. Screen readers, used by people who are blind or have low vision, read it aloud. Without it, a screen reader would read 672 unnamed boxes, and the grid would mean nothing to those users. It costs one attribute per cell and a couple of translation strings. Tests can also use it to find specific cells.

## Design 4: data flow

You have it right:
- **This PR:** the form's `schedule` ranges go to the wrapper, which runs `scheduleToSlotGrid` and passes a table of true/false slots to the grid.
- **#70:** a drag changes the slot table, the wrapper runs `slotGridToSchedule` (merging adjacent slots into ranges) and writes the result into the form, and the text fields and Save button see the change.

I've also noted that the reverse function belongs to #70, following the original spec.

# Plan: Weekly availability grid UI (sub-issue of #32)

## Context
Availability is entered today as text-field time ranges (`ScheduleComponent` → `DayRanges` → `TimeRangeField`). Issue #32 adds a When2Meet / Google Calendar style grid that users can drag across, with a toggle between the two input modes. **This PR only builds the grid as a visual element**: it renders the current availability. Drag (#70), the toggle (#71), and two-way sync and persistence (#73) come later.

Decisions from discussion:
- **Slot precision matches the text fields (15 minutes).** The grid has 96 rows per day, with a label on each hour. The text fields and the grid should look like mirror images of the same data.
- **Only one mode is visible at a time.** The grid takes the place of the text-field Schedule inside the same card. It doesn't sit beside it or stack with it. The toggle button is #71's job.

## Design

### 1. Shared slot interval
`INCREMENT` in `packages/features/schedules/components/ScheduleComponent.tsx:569` isn't exported. Move it into a small constants file that both components import, so the grid and the dropdowns can't drift apart:
- `packages/features/schedules/lib/constants.ts`: export `AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (same env var and the same default of 15).
- Change `ScheduleComponent.tsx` to import it. Behavior stays the same.

### 2. Pure conversion util (the basis for #70 and #73)
`packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts`:
- `getSlotsPerDay(intervalMinutes)`: returns 1440 / interval.
- `scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule: TimeRange[][], intervalMinutes): boolean[][]`. It returns 7 rows (Sunday = index 0, matching the form) of `slotsPerDay` booleans.
  - A slot is selected if it falls inside any range, using the **UTC** hour and minute from `start`/`end`. That's how the form stores times (see `useOptions` in `ScheduleComponent`).
  - An `end` at 23:59 fills the last slot.
  - Use native `Date` / `getUTCHours`, not Day.js, because this runs in a loop.
  - Cost is O(ranges + slots) per day: compute the start and end indices for each range, then fill that span.
- `resolveSlotInterval(interval)`: returns `interval` if it is a positive integer that divides 60 evenly (5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 60), otherwise 15. The conversion and the grid both call it, so a bad env value never breaks the layout.
- The reverse function (`slotGridToSchedule`, which merges adjacent slots into ranges) goes in this same file in #70. It's not part of this PR.

### 3. Presentational component
`packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`. It's controlled by props and doesn't depend on tRPC, so it can live in `features` and the platform atom can use it.
```ts
type WeeklyAvailabilityGridProps = {
  value: boolean[][];            // 7 × slotsPerDay, Sunday-indexed
  weekStart?: 0|1|2|3|4|5|6;     // display rotation only
  timeFormat: number | null;     // 12 / 24
  intervalMinutes?: number;      // defaults to the shared constant
  className?: string;
};
```
- **Layout:** a CSS grid with an hour-label column plus 7 day columns.
  - Day headers come from `weekdayNames(i18n.language, weekStart, "short")` (`packages/lib/weekday.ts`), and the day index is `(i + weekStart) % 7`, the same rotation `ScheduleComponent` uses.
  - Hour labels appear only on full-hour rows and are formatted per `timeFormat` (`packages/lib/timeFormat.ts`).
- **Cells:**
  - Selected: `bg-brand-default`. Unselected: `bg-default`.
  - Every hour boundary gets a solid `border-subtle` line. Every interval boundary inside the hour gets a faint dashed line: 3 per hour at 15 min, 1 at 30 min, none at 60 min.
  - Set `data-testid` and `data-selected` attributes for tests.
  - Add an `aria-label` per cell (day + time + "available"/"unavailable") so screen readers can describe each cell.
- **Height:** the hour height is fixed and slot height = hour height / slots per hour, so total grid height doesn't change with the interval. The hour height is taller on small screens (e.g. `h-12` per hour on desktop, `h-16` below `md`) so cells are easier to hit with a finger in #70.
- **Scrolling:** the body sits in a vertical scroll container (`max-h-[600px] overflow-y-auto`) with a sticky day header. It opens scrolled to midnight; auto-scrolling to a starting hour is out of scope.
- **Theme and mobile:**
  - Use semantic tokens only, so dark mode works automatically through `packages/config/theme/tokens.css`.
  - On narrow screens, columns shrink to `minmax(0,1fr)` with short day names. The label column stays narrow, and nothing scrolls horizontally.
- **Rendering cost:** 672 cells; wrap the component in `memo`.

### 4. Embedding in the page (the single swap point for #71)
In `packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx` (lines 668–701, the Schedule card):
- Add an optional prop `availabilityView?: "list" | "grid"` (default `"list"`). With `"grid"`, the card renders a thin wrapper that reads `useWatch({ name: "schedule" })`, converts it with `scheduleToSlotGrid`, and renders `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid` instead of `<Schedule>`.
- The default stays `"list"`, so platform-atom consumers and the live page don't change. #71 only needs to add the toggle and pass the prop down from `apps/web/modules/availability/[schedule]/schedule-view.tsx`.
- Replace the inline `indexOf` weekday array with `weekStartNum(weekStart)` (`packages/lib/weekstart.ts`) and reuse it for both components.

### 5. i18n
Add any new strings (cell aria-labels such as "available" / "unavailable", if those keys don't already exist) to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

## Files (about 6 code files, well under 500 lines)
- `packages/features/schedules/lib/constants.ts` (new)
- `packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts` (new) and `weekly-grid.test.ts` (new)

# Plan: Weekly availability grid UI (sub-issue of #32)

## Context
Availability is entered today as text-field time ranges (`ScheduleComponent` → `DayRanges` → `TimeRangeField`). Issue #32 adds a When2Meet / Google Calendar style grid with a toggle between the two input modes. **This PR only builds the grid as a read-only visual element** that shows the current availability. Drag-to-select and the reverse conversion are #70, the toggle is #71, and sync and persistence are #73.

Decisions so far:
- **Grid cells use the same slot interval as the text-field dropdowns.** That's 15 minutes by default (96 rows per day), with labels on the hour. If the interval doesn't divide 60 evenly, the grid falls back to 15.
- **Lines:** solid at each hour, faint dashed at each slot boundary inside the hour.
- **One mode visible at a time:** the grid replaces `<Schedule>` inside the same card when `availabilityView="grid"`. The default is `"list"`, so nothing changes on the live page.
- **Data flow:** the form's `schedule` field is the source of truth. A thin wrapper reads it, converts it with `scheduleToSlotGrid`, and passes the result to the grid.
- **Rows:** fixed hour height, so total grid height doesn't depend on the interval. Hours are taller below `md`.
- **Mobile:** no horizontal scroll. Vertical scrolling happens inside the grid, with a sticky day header. No auto-scroll to a starting hour.
- **Theme:** semantic theme color classes only, so dark mode is automatic. Selected cells use `bg-brand-default`.
- **Parity with the text fields:** the grid follows the user's week start and 12/24-hour format.
- **Accessibility:** an `aria-label` on each cell.

## Implementation order

The order goes from the bottom up: each step depends only on the steps before it, and each one compiles and passes its tests alone. If something breaks, the cause is in the step just added.

### Step 1. Extract the shared interval constant (refactor, no behavior change)
**Why first:** later steps import this constant, and doing it alone means any regression in the text fields shows up here, separate from the new code.

- **NEW** `packages/features/schedules/lib/constants.ts`
  ```ts
  export const AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES =
    Number(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AVAILABILITY_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL) || 15;
  ```
- **EDIT** `packages/features/schedules/components/ScheduleComponent.tsx:569`
  - Replace `const INCREMENT = …` with `import { AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES as INCREMENT } from "../lib/constants";`, placed with the other imports. That's one line changed, and the other uses of `INCREMENT` (lines 381 and 579) stay the same.
  - The dropdowns keep reading the raw value. Only the grid applies the divides-60 fallback, so text-field behavior is untouched.
- **Check:** the existing `parse-time-string.test.ts` still passes, and the dropdowns behave the same in `yarn dev`.

### Step 2. Pure conversion logic and its tests
**Why second:** it has no UI dependencies and the component needs it. Writing it and its tests before any rendering lets us confirm the data mapping (the hardest part to get right) on its own.

- **NEW** `packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts`
  - `resolveSlotInterval(interval: number): number`
    - Returns `interval` when it's an integer > 0 and `60 % interval === 0`, otherwise 15.
  - `getSlotsPerDay(interval: number): number`
    - Returns `1440 / resolveSlotInterval(interval)`.
  - `scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule: TimeRange[][], interval: number): boolean[][]`
    - Returns 7 arrays (Sunday = 0) of `slotsPerDay` booleans, all `false` to start. A missing day or an empty `[]` stays all `false`.
    - For each range: `startMin = getUTCHours*60 + getUTCMinutes`, and `endMin` is computed the same way.
    - If `endMin` is 1439 (23:59), treat it as 1440 so the last slot fills.
    - A slot `i` is selected when it overlaps the range: from `floor(startMin / interval)` up to, but not including, `ceil(endMin / interval)`. This is O(ranges + slots) per day and uses native `Date` only.
    - Using "overlap" means a range off the grid boundaries, like 9:10 at a 15-minute interval, still shows. With matching intervals, ranges always land on boundaries, so this only matters for the fallback case.
  - Types: `import type { TimeRange } from "@calcom/types/schedule"`.
- **NEW** `packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.test.ts`
  - `resolveSlotInterval`:
    - 15, 30, 60 and 5 pass through.
    - 0, -15, 7, 45, 120, NaN and 12.5 fall back to 15.
  - `getSlotsPerDay`: 96 at 15, 48 at 30, 24 at 60.
  - `scheduleToSlotGrid`:
    - An empty schedule gives all false.
    - 9:00–17:00 selects exactly slots 36–67.
    - 9:30–17:15 selects slots 38–68.
    - Two separate ranges on one day.
    - 0:00–23:59 selects all 96.
    - At a 30-minute interval, 9:00–17:00 selects slots 18–33.
    - Ranges are placed on the correct weekday index.
  - Build dates with `new Date(Date.UTC(1970, 0, 1, h, m))`, matching how the form stores times.
- **Check:** `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.test.ts`

### Step 3. Translation strings
**Why third:** the component's labels need these keys, and adding them first keeps step 4 type- and lint-clean the first time.

- **EDIT** `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`. Add near the other availability keys:
  - `"available": "Available"`. Only `"unavailable"` exists today, at line 312, so we reuse that one.
  - `"weekly_availability_grid": "Weekly availability"`, used as the grid's `aria-label`.
  - `"availability_grid_cell_label": "{{day}} {{time}}, {{status}}"`, used for each cell's `aria-label`.

### Step 4. The presentational component and its tests
**Why fourth:** it depends on steps 1–3, and the page can't embed it until it exists and is tested on its own.

- **NEW** `packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`
  - **Props:** `{ value: boolean[][]; weekStart?: 0..6; timeFormat: number | null; intervalMinutes?: number; className?: string }`.
    - `intervalMinutes` defaults to `AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES` and then goes through `resolveSlotInterval`.
  - **Day columns:** `weekdayNames(i18n.language, weekStart, "short")` from `@calcom/lib/weekday`. The data index is `(i + weekStart) % 7`, the same rotation as `ScheduleComponent.tsx:183-229`.
  - **Hour labels:** follow the same rule as the dropdowns (`ScheduleComponent.tsx:585`): `timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm"`, formatted 24 times with `dayjs.utc()`.
    - We deliberately don't use `getTimeFormatStringFromUserTimeFormat`, because it treats `null` as 12-hour while the dropdowns treat `null` as 24-hour. Matching the dropdowns keeps parity.
  - **Structure:**
    - An outer `div` with `role="grid"` and an `aria-label`, sitting inside `max-h-[600px] overflow-y-auto`.
    - A sticky header row, `sticky top-0 z-10 bg-default`, made of an empty corner cell plus 7 day names.
    - The body is a CSS grid with `grid-template-columns: auto repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr))`, so columns never force horizontal scroll.
    - Each label-column cell spans one hour.
    - Day cells:
      - Height is `calc(var(--hour-h) / slotsPerHour)`.
      - `--hour-h` is `4rem` by default and `3rem` from `md:` up, so rows are taller on mobile.
      - Selected cells are `bg-brand-default`, unselected `bg-default`.
      - Hour boundaries get a solid `border-t border-subtle`; slot boundaries inside the hour get a faint `border-t border-dashed border-subtle/50`.
      - Each cell has `data-testid="grid-cell-{day}-{slot}"`, `data-selected` and an `aria-label` from `t("availability_grid_cell_label", …)`.
  - **Styling:** classes are merged with `cn` from `@calcom/ui/classNames`, as `ScheduleComponent` does, and only semantic theme color classes are used.
  - **Performance:** export the component wrapped in `React.memo`. There are 672 cells at 15 minutes.
- **NEW** `packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.test.tsx`
  - It runs in the `@calcom/features` jsdom vitest project, and the setup already includes jest-dom.
  - Mock `useLocale` to return `{ t: (k) => k, i18n: { language: "en" } }` if the setup doesn't handle it.
  - Tests:
    - 7 day headers render in Sun…Sat order by default, and Mon…Sun when `weekStart = 1`.
    - 24 hour labels: "12:00am" first with `timeFormat=12`, "00:00" first with `24`.
    - At the default interval, 7 × 96 cells render; at 30, 7 × 48.
    - `data-selected` matches `value`, and selected cells get `bg-brand-default` while unselected ones don't.
    - With `weekStart=1`, the first column shows Monday's data (index 1).
- **Check:** `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/features/schedules`

### Step 5. Embed in the availability page
**Why last:** it's the only step that touches the shared page or atom, and it only connects pieces that are already tested.

- **EDIT** `packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx`
  - **New prop:** add `availabilityView?: "list" | "grid"` to the props type (near line 112), destructure it with a default of `"list"`, and pass it through.
  - **Wrapper:** a small local component in the same file, like the existing `DateOverride` local component:

```typescript
import type { TimeRange } from "@calcom/types/schedule";

const MINUTES_PER_DAY = 24 * 60;
const FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MINUTES = 15;
// The dropdowns offer 23:59 as the latest end time, meaning "end of day"
const END_OF_DAY_MINUTES = MINUTES_PER_DAY - 1;

/**
 * Grid cells must line up with hour boundaries so hour lines and labels never
 * fall inside a cell, so only intervals that divide an hour evenly are allowed.
 */
export function resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes: number): number {
  if (Number.isInteger(intervalMinutes) && intervalMinutes > 0 && 60 % intervalMinutes === 0) {
    return intervalMinutes;
  }
  return FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MINUTES;
}

export function getSlotsPerDay(intervalMinutes: number): number {
  return MINUTES_PER_DAY / resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes);
}

function toMinutesOfDay(date: Date): number {
  // Schedule times are stored as dates where only the UTC hour/minute are meaningful
  return date.getUTCHours() * 60 + date.getUTCMinutes();
}

/**
 * Converts the availability form's schedule (Sunday-indexed list of time ranges per day)
 * into a 7 × slotsPerDay matrix where `true` means the slot overlaps an available range.
 */
export function scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule: TimeRange[][], intervalMinutes: number): boolean[][] {
  const interval = resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes);
  const slotsPerDay = MINUTES_PER_DAY / interval;
  const grid: boolean[][] = [];

  for (let day = 0; day < 7; day++) {
    const slots = new Array<boolean>(slotsPerDay).fill(false);
    for (const range of schedule[day] ?? []) {
      const startMinutes = toMinutesOfDay(new Date(range.start));
      const rawEndMinutes = toMinutesOfDay(new Date(range.end));
      const endMinutes = rawEndMinutes === END_OF_DAY_MINUTES ? MINUTES_PER_DAY : rawEndMinutes;
      const firstSlot = Math.floor(startMinutes / interval);
      const lastSlotExclusive = Math.min(Math.ceil(endMinutes / interval), slotsPerDay);
      for (let slot = firstSlot; slot < lastSlotExclusive; slot++) {
        slots[slot] = true;
      }
    }
    grid.push(slots);
  }

  return grid;
}

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import type { TimeRange } from "@calcom/types/schedule";

import { getSlotsPerDay, resolveSlotInterval, scheduleToSlotGrid } from "./weekly-grid";

const time = (hours: number, minutes = 0) => new Date(Date.UTC(1970, 0, 1, hours, minutes));
const range = (start: Date, end: Date): TimeRange => ({ start, end });

const emptyWeek = (): TimeRange[][] => [[], [], [], [], [], [], []];

const selectedSlots = (slots: boolean[]) =>
  slots.reduce<number[]>((indices, isSelected, index) => {
    if (isSelected) indices.push(index);
    return indices;
  }, []);

const slotRange = (from: number, toInclusive: number) =>
  Array.from({ length: toInclusive - from + 1 }, (_, i) => from + i);

describe("resolveSlotInterval", () => {
  it.each([5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 60])("keeps %i because it divides an hour evenly", (interval) => {
    expect(resolveSlotInterval(interval)).toBe(interval);
  });

  it.each([0, -15, 7, 45, 120, Number.NaN, 12.5])("falls back to 15 for %s", (interval) => {
    expect(resolveSlotInterval(interval)).toBe(15);
  });
});

describe("getSlotsPerDay", () => {
  it.each([
    [15, 96],
    [30, 48],
    [60, 24],
    [7, 96],
  ])("returns the slot count for a %i minute interval", (interval, expected) => {
    expect(getSlotsPerDay(interval)).toBe(expected);
  });
});

describe("scheduleToSlotGrid", () => {
  it("returns 7 days of unselected slots for an empty schedule", () => {
    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(emptyWeek(), 15);

    expect(grid).toHaveLength(7);
    for (const day of grid) {
      expect(day).toHaveLength(96);
      expect(day.every((slot) => !slot)).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it("treats missing days as unavailable", () => {
    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid([], 15);

    expect(grid).toHaveLength(7);
    expect(grid.flat().some(Boolean)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("selects 9:00–17:00 as slots 36 through 67", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[1] = [range(time(9), time(17))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 15);

    expect(selectedSlots(grid[1])).toEqual(slotRange(36, 67));
  });

  it("handles ranges that start and end on quarter hours", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[2] = [range(time(9, 30), time(17, 15))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 15);

    expect(selectedSlots(grid[2])).toEqual(slotRange(38, 68));
  });

  it("selects multiple non-contiguous ranges on the same day", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[3] = [range(time(9), time(12)), range(time(13), time(17))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 15);

    expect(selectedSlots(grid[3])).toEqual([...slotRange(36, 47), ...slotRange(52, 67)]);
  });

  it("fills the final slot when a range ends at 23:59", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[0] = [range(time(0), time(23, 59))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 15);

    expect(grid[0].every(Boolean)).toBe(true);
  });

  it("selects any slot partially covered by a range", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[4] = [range(time(9, 10), time(9, 20))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 15);

    expect(selectedSlots(grid[4])).toEqual([36, 37]);
  });

  it("uses the given interval to size and fill slots", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[5] = [range(time(9), time(17))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 30);

    expect(grid[5]).toHaveLength(48);
    expect(selectedSlots(grid[5])).toEqual(slotRange(18, 33));
  });

  it("falls back to 15 minute slots for an invalid interval", () => {
    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(emptyWeek(), 45);

    expect(grid[0]).toHaveLength(96);
  });

  it("places ranges on the matching weekday index", () => {
    const schedule = emptyWeek();
    schedule[6] = [range(time(10), time(11))];

    const grid = scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule, 15);

    grid.forEach((day, index) => {
      expect(day.some(Boolean)).toBe(index === 6);
    });
  });
});

```typescript
import { memo, useMemo } from "react";

import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
import { weekdayNames } from "@calcom/lib/weekday";
import cn from "@calcom/ui/classNames";

import { AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES } from "../lib/constants";
import { getSlotsPerDay, resolveSlotInterval } from "../lib/weekly-grid";

export type WeeklyAvailabilityGridProps = {
  /** 7 × slotsPerDay matrix, Sunday-indexed, where `true` marks an available slot */
  value: boolean[][];
  weekStart?: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;
  timeFormat: number | null;
  intervalMinutes?: number;
  className?: string;
};

const DAYS_IN_WEEK = 7;
const GRID_COLUMNS = "grid grid-cols-[3.5rem_repeat(7,minmax(0,1fr))]";

function WeeklyAvailabilityGridComponent({
  value,
  weekStart = 0,
  timeFormat,
  intervalMinutes = AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES,
  className,
}: WeeklyAvailabilityGridProps) {
  const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
  const interval = resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes);
  const slotsPerDay = getSlotsPerDay(interval);
  const slotsPerHour = 60 / interval;

  const shortDayNames = useMemo(() => weekdayNames(i18n.language, weekStart, "short"), [i18n.language, weekStart]);
  const longDayNames = useMemo(() => weekdayNames(i18n.language, 0, "long"), [i18n.language]);

  // Same format rule as the time range dropdowns so both views read identically
  const slotLabels = useMemo(() => {
    const format = timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm";
    const startOfDay = dayjs.utc().startOf("day");
    return Array.from({ length: slotsPerDay }, (_, slot) =>
      startOfDay.add(slot * interval, "minute").format(format)
    );
  }, [timeFormat, slotsPerDay, interval]);

  const displayedDays = Array.from({ length: DAYS_IN_WEEK }, (_, column) => (column + weekStart) % DAYS_IN_WEEK);

  return (
    <div
      role="grid"
      aria-label={t("weekly_availability_grid")}
      aria-readonly="true"
      className={cn(
        "max-h-[600px] overflow-y-auto [--weekly-grid-hour-height:4rem] md:[--weekly-grid-hour-height:3rem]",
        className
      )}>
      <div role="row" className={cn(GRID_COLUMNS, "bg-default border-subtle sticky top-0 z-10 border-b")}>
        <div role="columnheader" aria-hidden="true" />
        {displayedDays.map((day, column) => (
          <div
            key={day}
            role="columnheader"
            aria-label={longDayNames[day]}
            className="text-default truncate py-2 text-center text-xs font-medium sm:text-sm">
            {shortDayNames[column]}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      {slotLabels.map((label, slot) => {
        const isHourStart = slot % slotsPerHour === 0;
        return (
          <div
            key={slot}
            role="row"
            className={GRID_COLUMNS}
            style={{ height: `calc(var(--weekly-grid-hour-height) / ${slotsPerHour})` }}>
            <div role="rowheader" className="text-muted pe-2 text-right text-xs leading-none">
              {isHourStart ? label : null}
            </div>
            {displayedDays.map((day) => {
              const isSelected = value[day]?.[slot] ?? false;
              return (
                <div
                  key={day}
                  role="gridcell"
                  data-testid={`weekly-grid-cell-${day}-${slot}`}
                  data-selected={isSelected}
                  aria-label={t("availability_grid_cell_label", {
                    day: longDayNames[day],
                    time: label,
                    status: t(isSelected ? "available" : "unavailable"),
                  })}
                  className={cn(
                    "border-subtle border-l",
                    isHourStart ? "border-t-subtle border-t" : "border-t-muted border-t border-dashed",
                    isSelected ? "bg-brand-default" : "bg-default"
                  )}
                />
              );
            })}
          </div>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}

export const WeeklyAvailabilityGrid = memo(WeeklyAvailabilityGridComponent);

export default WeeklyAvailabilityGrid;

import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { WeeklyAvailabilityGrid } from "./WeeklyAvailabilityGrid";

const emptyGrid = (slotsPerDay = 96) =>
  Array.from({ length: 7 }, () => new Array<boolean>(slotsPerDay).fill(false));

const columnHeaders = () =>
  screen
    .getAllByRole("columnheader")
    .map((header) => header.textContent)
    .filter(Boolean);

const hourLabels = () =>
  screen
    .getAllByRole("rowheader")
    .map((header) => header.textContent)
    .filter(Boolean);

describe("WeeklyAvailabilityGrid", () => {
  it("renders day headers starting on Sunday by default", () => {
    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={emptyGrid()} timeFormat={12} />);

    expect(columnHeaders()).toEqual(["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"]);
  });

  it("rotates day headers to the configured week start", () => {
    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={emptyGrid()} timeFormat={12} weekStart={1} />);

    expect(columnHeaders()).toEqual(["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]);
  });

  it("renders 24 hour labels in 12 hour format", () => {
    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={emptyGrid()} timeFormat={12} />);

    const labels = hourLabels();
    expect(labels).toHaveLength(24);
    expect(labels[0]).toBe("12:00am");
    expect(labels[13]).toBe("1:00pm");
  });

  it("renders 24 hour labels in 24 hour format", () => {
    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={emptyGrid()} timeFormat={24} />);

    const labels = hourLabels();
    expect(labels).toHaveLength(24);
    expect(labels[0]).toBe("00:00");
    expect(labels[23]).toBe("23:00");
  });

  it("renders one cell per day and slot for the given interval", () => {
    const { unmount } = render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={emptyGrid()} timeFormat={12} />);
    expect(screen.getAllByRole("gridcell")).toHaveLength(7 * 96);
    unmount();

    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={emptyGrid(48)} timeFormat={12} intervalMinutes={30} />);
    expect(screen.getAllByRole("gridcell")).toHaveLength(7 * 48);
  });

  it("styles cells according to their selected state", () => {
    const value = emptyGrid();
    value[1][36] = true;

    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={value} timeFormat={12} />);

    const selected = screen.getByTestId("weekly-grid-cell-1-36");
    const unselected = screen.getByTestId("weekly-grid-cell-1-35");
    expect(selected).toHaveAttribute("data-selected", "true");
    expect(selected.className).toContain("bg-brand-default");
    expect(unselected).toHaveAttribute("data-selected", "false");
    expect(unselected.className).not.toContain("bg-brand-default");
    expect(unselected.className).toContain("bg-default");
  });

  it("places each day's data under its rotated column", () => {
    const value = emptyGrid();
    value[1][0] = true;

    render(<WeeklyAvailabilityGrid value={value} timeFormat={12} weekStart={1} />);

    const firstRowCells = screen.getAllByRole("gridcell").slice(0, 7);
    expect(firstRowCells[0]).toHaveAttribute("data-testid", "weekly-grid-cell-1-0");
    expect(firstRowCells[0]).toHaveAttribute("data-selected", "true");
    expect(firstRowCells[6]).toHaveAttribute("data-testid", "weekly-grid-cell-0-0");
  });
});

11	In the cal.diy repo, on this user's Windows machine, `yarn type-check:ci --force` reliably fails with `Error: spawn tsc ENOENT` for every package it touches (confirmed identically for `@calcom/app-store`, `@calcom/ui`, and `@calcom/web`). This is not caused by any particular branch or code change — it reproduces the same way regardless of what files were edited.
12	
13	The root cause is that each package's `type-check:ci` script runs through `tsc-absolute` (a wrapper that rewrites TypeScript's reported paths to absolute paths), which internally calls Node's `child_process.spawn('tsc', [...])` directly rather than through a cross-platform-safe spawner. On Windows, the installed binary is actually `tsc.cmd`, and `child_process.spawn()` without `shell: true` does not resolve `.cmd`/`.bat` extensions the way a real shell does, so the spawn fails to find `tsc` at all.
14	
15	The plain `type-check` script (without `:ci`) runs `tsc --pretty --noEmit` directly via `yarn`, which correctly resolves the `.cmd` shim, and reports the same underlying type errors — it just skips the absolute-path rewriting convenience. So on this machine, prefer:
16	
17	```bash
18	yarn turbo run type-check --filter=<package> --force
19	```
20	
21	over `yarn type-check:ci --force`, when verifying type safety in this repo. This has been confirmed to actually run and pass on this machine, whereas `type-check:ci` cannot be used at all until the underlying `tsc-absolute`/Windows spawn issue is fixed upstream or worked around in the repo's tooling.
22
```

1	import type { TimeRange } from "@calcom/types/schedule";
2	
3	const MINUTES_PER_DAY = 24 * 60;
4	const FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MINUTES = 15;
5	// The dropdowns offer 23:59 as the latest end time, meaning "end of day"
6	const END_OF_DAY_MINUTES = MINUTES_PER_DAY - 1;
7	
8	/**
9	 * Grid cells must line up with hour boundaries so hour lines and labels never
10	 * fall inside a cell, so only intervals that divide an hour evenly are allowed.
11	 */
12	export function resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes: number): number {
13	  if (Number.isInteger(intervalMinutes) && intervalMinutes > 0 && 60 % intervalMinutes === 0) {
14	    return intervalMinutes;
15	  }
16	  return FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MINUTES;
17	}
18	
19	export function getSlotsPerDay(intervalMinutes: number): number {
20	  return MINUTES_PER_DAY / resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes);
21	}
22	
23	function toMinutesOfDay(date: Date): number {
24	  // Schedule times are stored as dates where only the UTC hour/minute are meaningful
25	  return date.getUTCHours() * 60 + date.getUTCMinutes();
26	}
27	
28	/**
29	 * Converts the availability form's schedule (Sunday-indexed list of time ranges per day)
30	 * into a 7 × slotsPerDay matrix where `true` means the slot overlaps an available range.
31	 */
32	export function scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule: TimeRange[][], intervalMinutes: number): boolean[][] {
33	  const interval = resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes);
34	  const slotsPerDay = MINUTES_PER_DAY / interval;
35	  const grid: boolean[][] = [];
36	
37	  for (let day = 0; day < 7; day++) {
38	    const slots = new Array<boolean>(slotsPerDay).fill(false);
39	    for (const range of schedule[day] ?? []) {
40	      const startMinutes = toMinutesOfDay(new Date(range.start));
41	      const rawEndMinutes = toMinutesOfDay(new Date(range.end));
42	      const endMinutes = rawEndMinutes === END_OF_DAY_MINUTES ? MINUTES_PER_DAY : rawEndMinutes;
43	      const firstSlot = Math.floor(startMinutes / interval);
44	      const lastSlotExclusive = Math.min(Math.ceil(endMinutes / interval), slotsPerDay);
45	      for (let slot = firstSlot; slot < lastSlotExclusive; slot++) {
46	        slots[slot] = true;
47	      }
48	    }
49	    grid.push(slots);
50	  }
51	
52	  return grid;
53	}
54
```

## The `yarn biome check` finding

**What Biome does:** it's the repo's formatter and linter in one tool. `yarn biome check <files>` does three things:
1. **Formats:** indentation, line wrapping, quotes.
2. **Lints:** checks the rules in `biome.json`. Each rule is set to `error`, `warn` or `off`.
3. **Organizes imports:** sorts and groups them.

With `--write`, it also applies the fixes it considers "safe" directly to the files. Without `--write`, it only reports.

**What happened when I ran `--write` on our 5 new files:**

| Change | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Re-sorted imports and Tailwind class names, re-wrapped long lines | Harmless, kept |
| Added `import process from "node:process";` to `constants.ts` | **Harmful, reverted** |
| Warned that exports should come after non-exported code (`useExportsLast`) in `weekly-grid.ts` | Fixed by hand: moved the private helper `toMinutesOfDay` above the exports |

**Why the `node:process` import is a problem.** The rule `noProcessGlobal` (a warning in `biome.json`) prefers importing `process` explicitly. But `NEXT_PUBLIC_AVAILABILITY_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL` is read in browser code. At build time, Next.js finds the literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_…` and replaces it with the actual value. It only does that when `process` is the global. Once `process` is an imported variable, Next.js leaves the expression alone. Then `node:process`, a Node-only module, ends up in the browser bundle. Best case the grid quietly falls back to 15 minutes; worst case the build fails. The original `ScheduleComponent.tsx` line used the global for this reason.

**The workaround:** `constants.ts` is back to using the global `process`, exactly like the original line. Going forward:
- Run `yarn biome check <files>` **without** `--write` first, or check `git diff` after `--write`.
- If the `node:process` import reappears, remove it.
- Optionally, add a `// biome-ignore lint/…/noProcessGlobal: Next.js must inline NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars from the global process` comment above the line so the auto-fix stops adding it. I haven't added it; your call.

**Not done yet:** Biome reported 7 warnings and 17 info notes in total, and I only saw part of the list. My follow-up command to print the rest was the one you stopped. So the remaining warnings haven't been reviewed.

**Don't confuse it with the type-check workaround** (from an earlier session). `yarn type-check:ci` fails on this Windows machine with `spawn tsc ENOENT`. Its wrapper can't find `tsc.cmd`. We use `yarn turbo run type-check --filter=@calcom/features --filter=@calcom/atoms --force` instead, and it passed (2/2 tasks).

### 3. `packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts` (new, logic only)
```ts
export function resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes: number): number {
  if (Number.isInteger(intervalMinutes) && intervalMinutes > 0 && 60 % intervalMinutes === 0) {
    return intervalMinutes;
  }
  return FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MINUTES; // 15
}

export function getSlotsPerDay(intervalMinutes: number): number {
  return MINUTES_PER_DAY / resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes); // 96 at 15 min
}
```
The core conversion:
```ts
for (const range of schedule[day] ?? []) {
  const startMinutes = toMinutesOfDay(new Date(range.start));   // UTC h*60 + m
  const rawEndMinutes = toMinutesOfDay(new Date(range.end));
  const endMinutes = rawEndMinutes === END_OF_DAY_MINUTES ? MINUTES_PER_DAY : rawEndMinutes;
  const firstSlot = Math.floor(startMinutes / interval);
  const lastSlotExclusive = Math.min(Math.ceil(endMinutes / interval), slotsPerDay);
  for (let slot = firstSlot; slot < lastSlotExclusive; slot++) slots[slot] = true;
}
```
- It reads UTC because the form stores times as dates where only the UTC hour and minute matter.
- 23:59 is treated as midnight so the last slot fills, matching the dropdown's "end of day" option.
- `floor` and `ceil` mean a partly covered slot still shows. That only matters if the interval fell back to 15.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 20:01:35Z)**_

There wasn't one earlier; I typed out the five new file paths by hand. Here are the options.

**Option 1: let git produce the file list (recommended for this branch).**
```bash
yarn biome check --files-ignore-unknown=true $(git diff --name-only HEAD; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)
```
- `git diff --name-only HEAD` lists tracked files you've modified: `ScheduleComponent.tsx`, `AvailabilitySettings.tsx`, `common.json`.
- `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists new untracked files (the five new ones), skipping anything in `.gitignore`.
- `--files-ignore-unknown=true` makes Biome skip file types it doesn't handle, like `schema.prisma`, instead of complaining about them.

This picks up `.specstory/` too if it has files Biome understands. Add `| grep -v '^.specstory'` inside the `$( … )` if that gets noisy.

Leave off `--write` the first time, so you see the findings before anything changes. That matters because of the `node:process` auto-fix.

**Option 2: Biome's built-in `--changed` / `--staged` flags.** These need git integration turned on, and this repo's `biome.json` has no `vcs` section, so you'd pass it on the command line:
```bash
yarn biome check --vcs-enabled=true --vcs-client-kind=git --vcs-use-ignore-file=true --vcs-default-branch=main --changed
```
There are two problems for this branch:
- `--changed` only sees files git already tracks, so it would **miss all five new files** until they're committed.
- You're on a detached `HEAD`, so comparing against `main` may not give the file list you expect.

`--staged` (after `git add`) does include new files. It's a good final check right before committing:
```bash
git add <your files>   # not schema.prisma

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 20:07:52Z)**_

I ran Biome without `--write` on the 8 changed and new files. **Nothing we introduced is an error.** The new files have a handful of small warnings that are easy to fix.

## What Biome reported
5 errors, 49 warnings, 107 info notes. To separate our changes from what was already there, I ran Biome on the original `HEAD` versions of the edited files and compared.

### The 5 errors are all line endings or already in the original code
| File | Error | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `common.json` | format | **Line endings only.** Git (`core.autocrlf=true`) checks files out with Windows line endings (CRLF), and Biome wants LF. With CRLF stripped there's no error. Git converts back to LF on commit, so it won't show up in the PR. |
| `ScheduleComponent.tsx` | format | Same CRLF cause; with CRLF stripped there's no error. |
| `ScheduleComponent.tsx` | organizeImports | Already in the original file. |
| `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` | format + organizeImports | Already in the original file, even with LF endings. |

### Warnings on edited files: no new warnings from us
- **`AvailabilitySettings.tsx`:** the original has exactly the same 34 warnings: 22 unsorted class lists, `forwardRef`, an over-long function, and so on.
- **`ScheduleComponent.tsx`:** same set as the original, minus the two `process.env` warnings, which moved with the line into `constants.ts`.

### Warnings on new files (ours)
| File | Warning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` | `useSortedClasses` ×4 | Tailwind class order only. `--write` doesn't apply this one; it needs `--unsafe`. |
| `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` | `noArrayIndexKey` | The rows use `key={slot}`, the array index. It's safe here because rows never reorder, but `key={label}` (e.g. `"9:15am"`, unique per row) clears it. |
| `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` | `useExportsLast` | The exported props type sits above private constants. Moving the two constants above it fixes this. |
| `constants.ts` | `noProcessGlobal`, `noProcessEnv` | Moved over from `ScheduleComponent.tsx`. These must stay as they are so Next.js can fill in `NEXT_PUBLIC_` for the browser. |
| `weekly-grid.ts`, both test files | none | |

## Suggested next step
I can clean up the three `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` warnings: sort the classes, use `key={label}`, and move the props type below the constants. Optionally I'll add a `biome-ignore` comment explaining the `process.env` line in `constants.ts`, so a future `--write` doesn't add the `node:process` import again. I'd leave the existing warnings in `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` and `ScheduleComponent.tsx` alone, since fixing them is unrelated cleanup that would bloat the PR.

Line 334 of `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` is still `availabilityView = "grid"`, so it still needs reverting to `"list"` before the PR.
