```typescript
import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
import { weekdayNames } from "@calcom/lib/weekday";
import cn from "@calcom/ui/classNames";
import { memo, useMemo, useRef } from "react";
import type { WeeklyGridSelectionChange } from "../hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag";
import { useWeeklyGridDrag } from "../hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag";
import { AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES } from "../lib/constants";
import { getSlotsPerDay, resolveSlotInterval } from "../lib/weekly-grid";

const DAYS_IN_WEEK = 7;
const GRID_COLUMNS = "grid grid-cols-[3.5rem_repeat(7,minmax(0,1fr))]";

type WeeklyAvailabilityGridProps = {
  /** 7 × slotsPerDay matrix, Sunday-indexed, where `true` marks an available slot */
  value: boolean[][];
  weekStart?: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;
  timeFormat: number | null;
  intervalMinutes?: number;
  className?: string;
  /** Makes the grid editable by drag; without it the grid is read-only */
  onSelectionChange?: (change: WeeklyGridSelectionChange) => void;
};

function WeeklyAvailabilityGridComponent({
  value,
  weekStart = 0,
  timeFormat,
  intervalMinutes = AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES,
  className,
  onSelectionChange,
}: WeeklyAvailabilityGridProps) {
  const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
  const interval = resolveSlotInterval(intervalMinutes);
  const slotsPerDay = getSlotsPerDay(interval);
  const slotsPerHour = 60 / interval;
  const isEditable = Boolean(onSelectionChange);

  const scrollContainerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const rowsRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const { getDisplaySlots, handlers } = useWeeklyGridDrag({
    value,
    intervalMinutes: interval,
    onSelectionChange,
    rowsRef,
    scrollContainerRef,
  });

  const shortDayNames = useMemo(
    () => weekdayNames(i18n.language, weekStart, "short"),
    [i18n.language, weekStart]
  );
  const longDayNames = useMemo(() => weekdayNames(i18n.language, 0, "long"), [i18n.language]);

  // Same format rule as the time range dropdowns so both views read identically
  const slotLabels = useMemo(() => {
    const format = timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm";
    const startOfDay = dayjs.utc().startOf("day");
    return Array.from({ length: slotsPerDay }, (_, slot) =>
      startOfDay.add(slot * interval, "minute").format(format)
    );
  }, [timeFormat, slotsPerDay, interval]);

  const displayedDays = Array.from(
    { length: DAYS_IN_WEEK },
    (_, column) => (column + weekStart) % DAYS_IN_WEEK
  );
  const displaySlotsByDay = displayedDays.map((day) => getDisplaySlots(day));

  return (
    <div
      ref={scrollContainerRef}
      role="grid"
      aria-label={t("weekly_availability_grid")}
      aria-readonly={!isEditable}
      className={cn(
        "max-h-[600px] overflow-y-auto [--weekly-grid-hour-height:4rem] md:[--weekly-grid-hour-height:3rem]",
        isEditable && "select-none",
        className
      )}>
      <div role="row" className={cn(GRID_COLUMNS, "sticky top-0 z-10 border-subtle border-b bg-default")}>
        <div role="columnheader" aria-hidden="true" />
        {displayedDays.map((day, column) => (
          <div
            key={day}
            role="columnheader"
            aria-label={longDayNames[day]}
            className="truncate py-2 text-center font-medium text-default text-xs sm:text-sm">
            {shortDayNames[column]}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div ref={rowsRef} role="rowgroup" {...(isEditable ? handlers : {})}>
        {slotLabels.map((label, slot) => {
          const isHourStart = slot % slotsPerHour === 0;
          return (
            <div
              key={label}
              role="row"
              className={GRID_COLUMNS}
              style={{ height: `calc(var(--weekly-grid-hour-height) / ${slotsPerHour})` }}>
              <div role="rowheader" className="pe-2 text-right text-muted text-xs leading-none">
                {isHourStart ? label : null}
              </div>
              {displayedDays.map((day, column) => {
                const isSelected = displaySlotsByDay[column][slot] ?? false;
                return (
                  <div
                    key={day}
                    role="gridcell"
                    data-testid={`weekly-grid-cell-${day}-${slot}`}
                    data-day={day}
                    data-slot={slot}
                    data-selected={isSelected}
                    aria-label={t("availability_grid_cell_label", {
                      day: longDayNames[day],
                      time: label,
                      status: t(isSelected ? "available" : "unavailable"),
                    })}
                    className={cn(
                      "border-subtle border-t border-l",
                      isHourStart ? "border-t-subtle" : "border-t-muted [border-top-style:dashed]",
                      isSelected ? "bg-brand-default" : "bg-default",
                      // Lets a finger drag select instead of scrolling; labels and header still scroll
                      isEditable && "cursor-pointer touch-none"
                    )}
                  />
                );
              })}
            </div>
          );
        })}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export const WeeklyAvailabilityGrid = memo(WeeklyAvailabilityGridComponent);

export default WeeklyAvailabilityGrid;
```

## What changed

**`packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`**
- **New optional prop:** `onSelectionChange`. **Without it, the grid behaves exactly as before:** read-only, no pointer handlers, `aria-readonly="true"`.
- **With it, the grid becomes editable:**
  - It calls `useWeeklyGridDrag` and attaches its pointer handlers to a new `rowgroup` wrapper around the slot rows. That wrapper is also what the hook measures to turn the pointer's Y position into a slot.
  - The grid gets `select-none`, which stops text highlighting, and `aria-readonly="false"`.
  - Each day cell gets `touch-none` and `cursor-pointer`. A finger drag on cells selects instead of scrolling, while the hour labels and day header keep normal touch scrolling.
  - Cells render from `getDisplaySlots(day)`, so the live preview shows during a drag.
- **New attributes:** cells have `data-day` / `data-slot`, which the hook reads to find the starting cell. The outer scroll box is passed to the hook for auto-scroll.

**`packages/features/schedules/test-utils/pointer-events.ts`** (new)
- The `PointerEvent` stand-in for jsdom now lives here, so both test files share it instead of duplicating it.
- It registers the class with `Object.defineProperty` rather than a type cast.

**`packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.test.tsx`**
- Imports the shared helper instead of defining it inline; no behavior change.

**`packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.test.tsx`**: 5 new tests.
- Without a handler: `aria-readonly="true"`, no `select-none`, no `touch-none`.
- With a handler: `select-none` on the grid, `touch-none` on cells but **not** on the hour labels.
- A drag through the real component highlights cells live (`bg-brand-default`) before release, then reports `{ day: 2, startMinute: 540, endMinute: 600, mode: "select" }`.
- Starting on a selected cell deselects.
- With Monday as the week start, the first column reports `day: 1`, so the day index survives the column rotation.

That's an editor-only problem, not a real error: the tests use `toHaveAttribute` and still pass. It's also not new. The merged #69 tests in this file used `toHaveAttribute` too, so those lines would have had the same red underline.

**Why it happens:**
1. **At runtime the matcher exists.** `toHaveAttribute` comes from `@testing-library/jest-dom`. The Vitest setup file (`packages/ui/components/test-setup.tsx`) registers it with `expect.extend(matchers)` before the tests run.
2. **TypeScript never learns about it.** `packages/features/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.*`, so test files aren't part of the package's TypeScript project, and nothing tells TypeScript that Vitest's `expect` has the extra jest-dom matchers. That's also why the command-line type check didn't report it: test files aren't checked there at all.
3. **VS Code checks the file anyway.** It falls back to a default setup where Vitest's `Assertion` type lacks `toHaveAttribute`, and flags each call.

This probably affects every test file in the repo that uses jest-dom matchers. I haven't checked them all.

**Options:**
1. **Leave it.** It matches how the rest of the repo works, and CI and tests are unaffected.
2. **Use plain Vitest assertions in our test files (recommended).** For example, `expect(cell.getAttribute("data-selected")).toBe("true")` instead of `toHaveAttribute`. Plain Vitest matchers are fully typed, so the underlines go away. That's about 15 one-line changes in `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.test.tsx`, including the #69 tests. The hook test file already uses `getAttribute`.
3. **Fix the typing repo-wide.** Add a type declaration that teaches Vitest's `expect` about the jest-dom matchers. That's the "proper" fix, but it's a cross-package config change outside this issue, so I'd only do it in its own PR.

Should I go ahead with option 2?

## What changed
**`packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx`** (+20 / −2). `WeeklyAvailabilityGridField` now passes `onSelectionChange` to the grid, so the grid becomes editable:
```ts
const handleSelectionChange = useCallback(
  ({ day, ...change }: WeeklyGridSelectionChange) => {
    const dayRanges = getValues(`schedule.${day}`) ?? [];
    setValue(`schedule.${day}`, applyDragToTimeRanges(dayRanges, change), { shouldDirty: true });
  },
  [getValues, setValue]
);
```
- **What a release does:**
  - It reads that day's current ranges from the form and applies the drag with Step 1's `applyDragToTimeRanges`, which only touches the dragged span.
  - It writes the result back to `schedule.<day>`, the same field the text fields use.
  - `shouldDirty` marks the form as changed, so Save enables.
- **Why `useCallback`:** it keeps the handler stable, so the memoized grid doesn't re-render when nothing changed.

## Correction about #69
The atoms package has no `type-check` script, so `turbo run type-check --filter=@calcom/atoms` skips `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` entirely. When I reported the #69 type check passing for both packages, the atoms side hadn't actually been checked. From now on I'll check this file with `tsc` directly. There are also two errors in `AvailabilitySettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx`, which is unrelated to our work. I haven't confirmed they exist on `main` too, but they concern API response types we never touched.

5. **Touch** (Chrome DevTools device mode): a finger drag on cells selects, and dragging on the hour labels scrolls.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 02:01:20Z)**_

This isn't caused by our change, and it doesn't break the build. It comes from the version of TypeScript VS Code is using.

**What I checked:**
- The repo's own TypeScript (5.9.3) reports **zero** of these `rootDir` errors when run on the atoms package.
- The flagged import, `@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/BookerStoreProvider`, was already in `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` before any of our PRs. The message lists about 35 other files importing it the same way. Every `@calcom/features/...` import in the atoms package gets this error in your editor, not just ours.

**Likely cause:** VS Code is checking the file with its **own bundled TypeScript**, not the repo's. The repo's `.vscode/settings.json` asks for the workspace version (`"typescript.tsdk": "node_modules/typescript/lib"`), but VS Code only switches after you approve it. Newer TypeScript versions (6.0 and later, if I remember right) changed how `rootDir` is inferred when `outDir` is set: it defaults to the folder containing `tsconfig.json`. The atoms `tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` and pulls in files from `../../features`, so a newer TypeScript complains that those files are outside the atoms folder. I'm fairly but not fully sure about the exact version where that default changed, and I couldn't read your VS Code's bundled version from here.

**Fix (editor only, no code change):**

## Follow-up issue draft (long-press)

```markdown
### Summary
Use long-press to start a drag on touch devices in the weekly availability grid.

### Problem
Since #70, a finger on a grid cell always selects (`touch-action: none` on cells). On phones the grid takes up most of the screen, so users trying to scroll the page or the grid by touching a cell select slots by accident. Scrolling currently only works from the hour-label column or the day header, which isn't obvious.

### Proposed solution
Match Google Calendar mobile:
- A normal swipe on the grid scrolls.
- Holding a cell still for about 350ms starts a drag, with visual feedback on the starting cell; then dragging selects or deselects as in #70.
- Mouse behavior is unchanged (drag starts immediately).

### Implementation notes
- Logic belongs in `packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`: on a touch `pointerdown`, start a timer instead of a drag; cancel it if the finger moves more than about 8px first, or if the browser takes over scrolling (`pointercancel`).
- Once a drag starts, block native scrolling with a non-passive `touchmove` listener (`{ passive: false }`); React's touch handlers can't do this.
- Cells need `touch-action: pan-y` instead of `none`, and the long-press context menu / iOS callout must be suppressed.
- Tests: Vitest fake timers for the hold threshold and movement cancel; real scrolling must be verified on a device or in Chrome DevTools touch emulation.

### Out of scope
Keyboard selection.
```

## PR A

**Title:** `feat(schedules): add drag selection and range editing logic for weekly grid`

```markdown
## What does this PR do?

Part of #70 (1 of 3; followed by the drag hook PR and the grid wiring PR).

Adds the pure logic behind drag-to-select on the weekly availability grid. It has no UI and doesn't change the app's behavior yet.

### What changed and why
All changes are in `packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts`.

- **`applyDragToSlots(slots, anchorSlot, currentSlot, mode)`** computes the live preview. Every slot between the starting slot and the current slot, in either direction, becomes selected or unselected. It doesn't modify the input.
- **`applyDragToTimeRanges(ranges, { startMinute, endMinute, mode })`** applies a finished drag to one day's `{start, end}` ranges. **It only changes what the dragged span touches:**
  - **select:** merges with ranges it touches or overlaps (`6–7` + drag `7–8` → `6–8`).
  - **deselect:** clips, removes or splits ranges (`9–13` minus `11–12` → `9–11` + `12–13`).
  - Ranges outside the span are returned unchanged, so custom times like `9:10` and the user's own rows in the text fields survive.
  - We chose this over rebuilding the day from grid slots, which would silently snap off-grid times (`9:10` → `9:00`) anywhere in the day.
  - New times are built on today's UTC date, with end of day as `23:59:59.999`. That's the same format the time dropdowns and the server transformer use, so the dropdowns recognize the values.
- **`getAutoScrollSpeed(pointerY, top, bottom)`** returns scroll speed near the grid's edges, used by the drag hook in the next PR.
- **New types:** `SlotDragMode` and `SlotSelectionChange`.
- **Small refactor:** shared "minutes since midnight" helpers. `scheduleToSlotGrid` behaves the same, and its existing tests are unchanged.
```

## PR B

**Title:** `feat(schedules): add pointer drag hook with edge auto-scroll for weekly grid`

```markdown
## What does this PR do?

Part of #70 (2 of 3; depends on PR A, base branch `feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic`).

Adds `useWeeklyGridDrag`, the React hook that turns mouse, touch and pen input into grid selections. Nothing uses it yet; the next PR wires it into the grid.

### What changed and why
`packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.ts` (new):
- **Pointer Events:** mouse, touch and pen are handled by one set of handlers instead of separate mouse and touch code.
- **On press:**
  - Ignored for non-left mouse buttons, secondary touches, and when the grid is read-only (no `onSelectionChange`).
  - Otherwise: `preventDefault()` (no text selection or native drag ghost), capture the pointer, and set the mode from the starting cell. An empty cell means select; a filled cell means deselect.
- **On move:** the slot comes from the pointer's **Y position** relative to the rows, clamped to the day, and X is ignored.
  - This enforces the issue's "primary drag direction only" rule: a drag stays in its starting day's column.
  - It also keeps working when the pointer leaves the grid during auto-scroll.
  - It only re-renders when the slot actually changes.
- **On release:** reports `{ day, startMinute, endMinute, mode }` once, if anything changed. **On cancel:** the preview is discarded.
- **Edge auto-scroll:** `useEdgeAutoScroll`, an internal hook. While dragging within 40px of the grid's top or bottom edge, it scrolls each animation frame and re-checks the slot under the stationary pointer, so a whole day can be selected in one drag. It stops on release, cancel and unmount.
- **`getDisplaySlots(day)`:** returns the live preview for the dragged day and the committed slots for every other day.
```

Can you please explain what exactly is going on with the stacked PR thing?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 02:14:45Z)**_

## The idea in one sentence
A pull request shows the difference between its branch and its **base** branch. Stacking means pointing each PR's base at the **previous PR's branch** instead of `main`, so each PR shows only its own piece.

## Your commits today
Your four commits sit in a line on top of `main`:

```
main ── 7c80 (logic) ── 08a1 (hook) ── 4153 (grid) ── 1d9d (form wiring)
```

A **branch is just a named label pointing at one commit**. Creating the two new branches doesn't copy or change any code; it only adds labels at points already in that line:

```
main ── 7c80 ── 08a1 ── 4153 ── 1d9d
         ▲       ▲               ▲
         A       B               C (your current branch)
```

## Why not just open three PRs against `main`?
Each branch contains everything before it. Against `main`:
- PR A would show the logic ✔
- PR B would show logic **+** hook (A's work again)
- PR C would show logic + hook + grid + wiring, the whole 1,100 lines

Reviewers would see the same code up to three times, and the size problem wouldn't be solved.

## What stacking does
Set each PR's base to the branch below it:

| PR | Branch | Base | Diff shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | A | `main` | only the logic commit (~390 lines) |
| B | B | **A** | only the hook commit (~480 lines) |
| C | C | **B** | only the grid and wiring commits (~275 lines) |

Each PR is small and reviewable on its own, while the code still builds on what came before.

## How merging works
They must merge **in order**:
1. **Merge A into `main`.** The logic is now in `main`.
2. **B's base moves to `main`.** GitHub does this automatically when A's branch is deleted after merging. B's diff still shows only the hook, because the logic is already in `main`.
3. **Merge B, then C**, the same way.

After that, `main` has all four commits, exactly as if you'd merged one big PR.

## Things to watch for
1. **Changes requested on an earlier PR.** Say a reviewer asks for a change on A. You commit the fix on branch A, but B and C were built before it, so they don't have it. Bring it forward by **merging**, not rebasing (the repo rules say not to force-push shared branches):
   ```bash
   git switch feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook && git merge feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic && git push
   git switch feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction && git merge feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook && git push
   ```
2. **Squash merging breaks stacks.** If A were squash-merged, `main` would get a *new* commit with the same changes, and B would still contain the old one. That leads to duplicated diffs or conflicts. Your repo's history ("Merge pull request #84") shows it uses regular merge commits, so this shouldn't happen. If someone picks "Squash and merge" on A, tell me and we'll sort out B.
3. **Merge in order.** Merging C first would bring A and B in with it, unreviewed. Marking PRs B and C "Depends on #A" in their descriptions helps prevent that.
4. **CI checks** on B and C run against their base branch, which is normal.

## The simpler alternative
Open only **PR A** now. When it merges, open B against `main`, and then C. There's no stacking and nothing to keep in sync, but it's slower: each review waits for the previous merge, and reviewers can't see where the work is heading.

Stacking is the usual choice when the pieces are already done, as yours are, and the extra steps only come up if a reviewer asks for changes on A or B.

Here are the commands, run from the repo root in your terminal. `gh` isn't installed, so the PRs themselves are opened in the GitHub website.

## Part 1: Check your starting point

```bash
git switch feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction
```
Makes sure you're on your #70 branch, the one holding all four commits. You should already be on it; this just confirms it.

```bash

```
Shows uncommitted changes. You should see only `.vscode/settings.json`, `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` and `ai-logs/...`. **Leave them alone.** Nothing below commits or pushes uncommitted changes, so they stay local.

```bash
git log --oneline -5
```
Lists your latest commits. Confirm the four #70 commits are there, newest first:
```
1d9d935325 feat(availability): commit weekly grid drags to the schedule form
415352035a feat(schedules): make weekly availability grid editable by drag
08a1fb2df7 feat(schedules): add pointer drag hook with edge auto-scroll for weekly grid
7c80e354ab feat(schedules): add drag selection and range editing logic for weekly grid
8c03587f1c Merge pull request #84 ...
```

## Part 2: Create the two lower branches

```bash
git branch feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic 7c80e354ab
```
Creates a branch named `feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic` that points at the **logic** commit.
- `git branch <name> <commit>` only creates a label at that commit; it doesn't switch you to it or copy any files.
- This branch contains everything up to and including the logic commit: `main` plus Step 1.

```bash
git branch feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook 08a1fb2df7
```
Same thing for the **hook** commit. This branch contains `main` + Step 1 + Step 2.

The **top** of the stack needs no new branch: your current branch `feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction` already points at the last commit, so it holds Steps 1–4.

```bash
git log --oneline --decorate -5
```
Same list as before, but `--decorate` shows which branch labels sit on which commit. Check it looks like this:
```
1d9d935325 (HEAD -> feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction) feat(availability): ...
415352035a feat(schedules): make weekly availability grid editable by drag
08a1fb2df7 (feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook) feat(schedules): add pointer drag hook ...
7c80e354ab (feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic) feat(schedules): add drag selection ...
```

## Part 3: Push all three branches to GitHub

```bash
git push -u origin feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction
```
- `push` uploads the branches' commits to GitHub.
- `origin` is the GitHub repo (`CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy`).
- `-u` remembers each local branch's GitHub counterpart, so a later plain `git push` or `git pull` on that branch knows where to go.
- Listing all three pushes them in one go. Only committed work is uploaded, so the files you left alone stay local.

## Part 4: Open the three PRs on GitHub

Order matters, because each PR needs the branch below it to exist on GitHub, which Part 3 took care of. These links open GitHub's "compare" page with the base and branch already filled in.

**PR A** (base `main`):
`https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/compare/main...feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic`

**PR B** (base: branch A):
`https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/compare/feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic...feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook`

**PR C** (base: branch B):
`https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/compare/feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook...feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction`

The URL format is `compare/<base>...<your branch>`. GitHub shows only the changes in "your branch" that aren't in "base", which is what makes each PR small.

On each page:
1. **Check the file list.** A should show 2 files, B 2 files, and C 5 files. If C shows 8, its base is wrong.
2. Paste in the title and description from the matching draft. Once A exists, add "Depends on #<A's number>" to B, and "Depends on #<B's number>" to C.
3. Click the arrow next to **Create pull request** and pick **Create draft pull request**, per the repo rules.

## Part 5: After review, merge in order

1. **Merge PR A** with **"Create a merge commit"**, not "Squash and merge". Squashing would break the stack. Then delete branch A when GitHub offers. GitHub then switches PR B's base to `main` automatically.
2. **Merge PR B** the same way, and delete its branch. PR C's base switches to `main`.
3. **Merge PR C.** It contains "Closes #70", so the issue closes automatically.

If a reviewer asks for changes on A or B, commit the fix on that branch and carry it upward with `git merge`, as shown earlier. Never force-push.

## Part 6: Back on your machine, afterwards

```bash
git switch main
git pull
```
Switches to `main` and downloads everything merged in the meantime, including your three PRs, so your next issue starts from up-to-date code.

Here's the draft, following `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md` section by section. The template applies the `✨ feature` and `🚨 needs approval` labels for you, and I kept its "House rules" footer.

**Title:** `feat(availability): long-press to start drag on touch devices in the weekly availability grid`

```markdown
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Since #70, the weekly availability grid supports drag-to-select with mouse and touch. On touch devices, a finger on any day cell **always** starts a selection, because the cells use `touch-action: none` so the browser doesn't scroll while dragging.

On a phone the grid fills most of the screen. A user who puts a finger on the grid to **scroll** (the page, or the grid's own 600px scroll area) selects or deselects time slots by accident. Scrolling currently only works by dragging on the hour-label column or the day header, which users aren't likely to discover.

As an event host on a phone, I'm frustrated when I try to scroll through my week and end up changing my availability instead.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Use **long-press to start a drag on touch input**, the way Google Calendar's mobile app works:

- **Swipe** on the grid: scrolls normally (page or grid), with no selection.
- **Press and hold** a cell for about 350ms without moving: the starting cell highlights to show a drag has started. Dragging then selects or deselects exactly as in #70: the starting cell's state sets the mode, the drag stays in that day's column, and the grid auto-scrolls near its edges.
- **Mouse and pen:** unchanged, the drag starts immediately on press.

Acceptance criteria:
1. On touch devices, a quick swipe starting on a grid cell scrolls and never changes the selection.
2. On touch devices, holding a cell for about 350ms, then dragging, selects or deselects slots with the same behavior as #70, including auto-scroll.
3. Once a long-press drag has started, the page and grid don't scroll under the finger, except for the grid's own edge auto-scroll.
4. A long press doesn't open the browser's context menu, the iOS callout, or a text selection.
5. Mouse behavior is unchanged.
6. Automated tests cover the hold threshold, cancelling on movement, and mouse versus touch behavior.

Implementation notes (from the #70 design):
- **Where:** the logic belongs in `packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`.
- **Starting the timer:** on a touch `pointerdown`, start a timer instead of a drag. Cancel it if the finger moves more than about 8px first, or if the browser takes over scrolling (it fires `pointercancel`).
- **Blocking scroll once dragging:** add a native `touchmove` listener with `{ passive: false }` that calls `preventDefault()`. React's touch handlers are passive and can't do this.
- **Cell styles:** change `touch-none` to `touch-pan-y` on day cells in `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` so swipes scroll, and suppress the long-press menu (`onContextMenu` → `preventDefault`, `-webkit-touch-callout: none`).
- **Testing:** use Vitest fake timers for the threshold logic. Real scrolling can't be simulated in jsdom, so it needs a manual check on a device or in Chrome DevTools touch emulation.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Keep the current behavior** (cells select, labels scroll). This shipped in #70 because it's simple, but it's prone to accidental selection and the scroll area is hard to discover.
- **An "Edit" toggle** that turns on drag mode, with scrolling everywhere otherwise. Clear, but it adds an extra tap and UI state every time.
- **Two-finger scroll and one-finger select.** Not a common pattern, and hard to discover.
- **Dragging only after a horizontal or vertical movement threshold.** That conflicts with vertical scrolling, because drags in this grid are vertical too.

Long-press matches a pattern users already know from calendar apps, so it seems the most intuitive.

### Additional context

- Builds on #70 (drag-to-select). PRs: #<PR A>, #<PR B>, #<PR C>.
- Related: #71 (grid/list toggle). The grid isn't visible to users until that lands, so this is a usability fix before release rather than an urgent bug.
- Out of scope: keyboard-based selection, and any change to mouse behavior.

### Requirement/Document

- [Pointer Events: `pointercancel` and `touch-action`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Pointer_events)
- [Passive event listeners and `preventDefault`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener#passive)

---

##### House rules

- If this issue has a `🚨 needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.
  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `🚨 needs approval` label.

  - Follow Best Practices lined out in our [Contributor Docs](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
```
